newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unchanged, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unchanged, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices in late afternoon trade on Monday remained around flat as the market wound down ahead of the holidays, though traders said there was some light retail interest.
"The market was unchanged, there was some investment business going on, but very little dealer-to-dealer business being done," a trader said.
Fixed-income markets have recovered from lows seen in May and June, though the benchmark U.S. Treasury remains below highs seen early this year.
Still, traders said tax-related selling, which can be a major feature in the municipal market, largely has been absent.
"There's very little interest in the marketplace, they've been no bid-wanted lists, and no compelling tax-losses to take," the trader added.

Other factors curbing activity were the large number of traders who were taking the week of Christmas off, as well as the short supplies of cash available because companies are starting to close their books for the year-end.

Few issuers appeared willing to take their chances in the thin markets, as only $20 million of competitive and negotiated sales are scheduled for this week. Though this is slightly higher than first expected, it marks a sharp retreat from last week's approximately $3.14 billion of new issues.
The largest competitive issue, Janesville, Wisconsin's general obligation promissory notes, fetched a net interest cost of 4.84 percent, Firstar Bank said.

Two negotiated offerings expected this week total $15 million, though the largest sale in this category, a $63 million New York State Environmental Facilities Corp offering instead was priced on Friday.
Eleven issue totaling $406 million are on the Reuters possible negotiated calendar, meaning underwriters have said they might price the deals during the week depending on market conditions.

The March municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade eased one tick to 116-8/32, while the March U.S. Treasury futures firmed five ticks to 112-30/32. The MOB spread fattened to plus 106 ticks.

Actively quoted issues included Denver Colorado City & County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.75 percent, NET, one basis point higher than quotes seen on Friday.
And Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues of June 2027, which have a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.74 percent, NET, down three basis points.
